Lair 2.0.1 — the first build published to the release channel.

Until now Lair was installed by a script that overwrote `/Applications/Lair.app`
on the machine it was built on. This is the same app, packaged so it can be
handed to somebody else and kept current by Depot.

**Installing**

- Unzip and drag to Applications, or let [Depot](../depot/) do it — Depot
  replaces the bundle atomically and quits a running copy first, which a manual
  drag does not.
- Your board lives in `~/.undercurrent/lair/db/lair.db` and is untouched by an
  update. It is one SQLite file: copying it is a backup.

**First launch**

This build is ad-hoc signed rather than notarised, so macOS asks once. Open
**System Settings → Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**. Installing
through Depot skips this entirely — a Depot install carries no quarantine flag.

**Note on size**

180 MB unpacked. Lair is a Compose Desktop app and ships its own Java runtime, so
the download is what it is. Nothing is downloaded at first run.
